html:
A war from 113 to 101 BCE between the Roman Republic and migrating peoples from the north, the Cimbri and Teutons, with Celtic allies. It was the worst threat to Italy since Hannibal.

The Cimbri and Teutons came from around Jutland and wandered for years through central Europe and Gaul, looking for land. Rome met them again and again and lost:

  • at Noreia in the eastern Alps in 113 BCE;
  • in southern Gaul in 109 and 107 BCE;
  • at Arausio (Orange) in 105 BCE, the worst Roman defeat since Cannae.

In panic, Romans elected Gaius Marius consul year after year. He trained a new army, open to men without property (the Marian reforms). Luckily for Rome the migrants turned towards Spain for a time. When they came back, Marius destroyed the Teutons at Aquae Sextiae in 102 BCE, and with Catulus destroyed the Cimbri at Vercellae in 101 BCE.

Later Romans counted this as the first of their long wars with the Germanic peoples, though the Cimbri may have been partly Celtic.
sum: A war from 113 to 101 BCE between the Roman Republic and migrating peoples from the north, the Cimbri and Teutons, with Celtic allies. It was the worst threat to Italy since Hannibal.
